expectations.text: Uses 3 training days per week with glute work each day
Balances horizontal (thrust/bridge), vertical (squat/deadlift/lunge) and lateral/rotary (abduction) exercises across the week
Mixes heavy (1-5), medium (6-12) and light/high-rep (13+) work
Places big lifts (hip thrust, squat or deadlift) first in sessions and pump/abduction work last
Ramps effort across the 4 weeks (easier week 1, hardest week 4) or otherwise programs a deload
Gives specific sets x reps and effort targets (RIR/RPE or to-failure guidance)
Explains how to progress (beat reps/load, log numbers)
Says the standard flat bench (~16 in+) is likely too high and suggests a lower setup around 12 in for her height
Suggests moving the feet farther out (shins roughly vertical at the top) to reduce quads
Suggests driving through the heels
Suggests adding a band around the knees
Addresses low back: ribs down / posterior pelvic tilt at lockout / chin tucked, avoiding lumbar hyperextension
Mentions the American hip thrust or bench-position fix (bottom of shoulder blades at bench edge)
Identifies too much volume / too little effort and recommends cutting weekly glute volume and frequency (e.g., 2-3 days, fewer sets)
Recommends pushing sets closer to failure (effort over volume)
Recommends deloads or fluctuating training stress
Recommends glute-dominant exercises (barbell glute bridge, hip thrust variations, abduction) to grow glutes without thighs
Recommends reducing quad/hamstring-dominant exercises (squats, lunges, leg press, etc.)
Notes thigh size is often fat rather than muscle and addresses diet/protein
Mentions progressive overload / tracking strength on a main lift
